name: KGW watermarking: hash the previous token, split the vocabulary in half, promote green tokens - and the decode-time cost is dominated by the vocabulary permutation
symptom: Serving a watermarked model either 'costs nothing' or is unbearably slow, and the difference is the vocabulary permutation, not the logit bias. A delta of a few hundredths on quality is easy; a randperm over a 150k-token vocabulary on every decode step is not.
root_cause: KGW (Kirchenbauer et al.) partitions the vocabulary per token: hash the previous token, seed a PRNG, split the vocabulary into equal green and red lists, softly promote green tokens during sampling, detect with a one-proportion z-test that needs no model access. Detection is cheap and needs only the secret key. The insertion cost is the partitioning: KGW's per-token membership complexity is O(V log V) because it requires a vocabulary permutation via randperm, repeated at every decode step for every batch row. Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking reduces membership to a single comparison against a counter-based RNG, O(1) per token, reporting under 1% end-to-end generation overhead at all batch sizes on a Qwen3-8B (vocab 151,936) at temperature 1.0 with a single RTX 3090. SynthID-Text sits in between at O(k*m) with m=30 tournament reweighting passes.
workaround: If you must watermark, prefer a stateless formulation over a vocabulary permutation. If you serve SynthID, note that the tournament depth is a direct per-token cost knob (m reweighting passes) and that its own analysis shows the mean detection score degrades as layers increase - so the layers you add for robustness are the ones costing you speed and detection power.
notes: COST NUMBERS ARE NARROWLY SOURCED. The O(V log V) vs O(1) vs O(k*m) comparison and the sub-1% end-to-end figure are SBW's own measurements on consumer hardware at temperature 1.0 with pure sampling - not a server benchmark, and not a batched multi-tenant one. Nobody has published a watermarking overhead figure for a production serving stack under continuous batching. Treat the DIRECTION (permutation is the expensive part) as solid and the magnitude as unestablished.
